name: iris_ring
title: Iris Ring - annular WS2812C-2020 LED board behind each iris of Iris (B3, fitted twice)
brief: Iris board B3, fitted twice: an 18 mm annulus with a key flat 8.4 mm from the centre and a 7.6 mm hole for the camera lens, 0.8 mm thick, 2 layers, that glows behind the translucent iris of each eye. Twelve Worldsemi WS2812C-2020-V1 RGB LEDs on r = 6.6 mm at 15 deg + 30 deg k face the iris on the front, chained clockwise from the first LED beside the wire pads; each has its own 100 nF on the back. The RING harness lands on four 1.0 mm back-side pads at the temporal edge (P1 5V_LED, P2 LED_DIN, P3 GND, P4 GND), with a 33 ohm series resistor into the first DIN and 4.7 uF of bulk. The back's centre 8.7 mm square rests on the camera holder and carries no parts.

blocks.title: RING wire pads, DIN series R, bulk C

netClasses.name: LED_PWR
netClasses.why: the ring's supply: 12 LEDs x 3 channels x 5 mA plus 12 x 0.5 mA quiescent = 186 mA at full white (WS2812C-2020-V1 datasheet p.1 and p.3). 0.3 mm still enters the LEDs' 0.7 mm pads; the current budget keeps the route ladder from narrowing it

rules.why: 0.15 mm clearance and 0.2 mm tracks inside JLC's 2-layer line (0.10 / 0.10 mm, jlcpcb_2layer); 0.5 / 0.3 mm vias fit between the LEDs' inner pads (r >= 5.08) and the hole's clearance ring (r <= 4.1); every class is 0.2 mm or wider, so 0.15 leaves room for Freerouting's rounding
rules.why_edge: 0.3 mm copper to edge, not the 0.5 mm of the other boards: D9 and D10 reach 0.76 mm from the key flat, so at 0.5 mm no ground track passed below them and the router ran GND between the LEDs, leaving DIN11 open (measured on this brief); at 0.3 mm it routes 64 -> 0. Confirm 0.3 mm against the fab's routed-edge rule before ordering

keepouts.name: camera_holder_contact
keepouts.why: spec 4.4: the back's centre 8.7 x 8.7 mm square rests on the 8.5 x 8.5 mm camera holder (left eye: the dummy carrier); 0.1 mm margin. Tracks and vias may pass under it

keepouts.name: name_window
keepouts.why: keeps the back's only free band (between C9/C10 and the key flat) clear of vias for the board name; tracks may cross it

board.notes: Outline from spec 4.4 (binding): circle 18.0 mm, key flat 8.4 mm from the centre (the chord y = 17.4 of the frame), centre hole 7.6 mm. The polygon's corners are tangent points of the circle and their 9 mm fillets are exact arcs of it. Board thickness 0.8 mm is an order option at the fab: the pipeline has no thickness setting, and its gerber job and STEP carry KiCad's default 1.6 mm stackup.

in:R?.why: 33 ohm DIN series resistor between the wire pads and C1/C12, pad 1 (LED_DIN) up toward P2, pad 2 (DIN1) down into the gap between D12 and D1

in:C?.why: 4.7 uF bulk beside P1 (5V_LED), in line with C1, its pad 1 (5V_LED) facing C1's pad 1

route.why: every part is locked; the route stage measures Freerouting with fanout on and off and keeps the better solve; the outline is stated and shaped, so it is never grown

silk.why: the board's name on the back, as two words under C9 and C10 in the via-free band above the key flat (read from the back: Iris on the left, Ring on the right). As a silk.title line it never landed: the designator pass runs first and seats C9's and C10's designators in that band, the only free space on the back, while words are placed before designators. No other silk words: the wire pads' labels found no free spot at 2.1 mm pitch, so the pad order is in the README
